convertibility_reason: Uses external .mqh libraries (martingail.mqh, ontesterfunctions.mqh) for position sizing and tester metrics. Martingale money management adds complexity beyond simple fixed/fractional sizing.

long.left: Fast TriX[0] < Fast TriX[1] AND Fast TriX[1] > Fast TriX[2]

short.left: Fast TriX[0] > Fast TriX[1] AND Fast TriX[1] < Fast TriX[2]

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Martingail class manages lot sizing via global variables; shape (DML=1000) sets base deposit fraction, DoublingCount (Ud=1) controls martingale multiplier on loss

custom_logic_notes: Long entry: Fast TriX V-bottom (t[0]>t[1] && t[1]<t[2]) confirmed by Slow TriX rising (k[1]>k[0]). Short entry: Fast TriX inverted-V top (t[0]<t[1] && t[1]>t[2]) confirmed by Slow TriX falling (k[1]<k[0]). Uses CopyBuffer with shift=1 reading bars [1],[2],[3] as indices [0],[1],[2]. OnTester returns profitc_divide_lossc / (max_series_loss+1) with guard that Tp>=Stop. Martingale state persisted via global variables (MG_2).
python_conversion_notes: TriX indicator must be reimplemented (triple EMA of log price differences). Martingail class from martingail.mqh needs reverse-engineering or reimplementation; it persists state via MT5 global variables which have no Python equivalent — use file-based or dict-based state persistence. ontesterfunctions.mqh provides profitc_divide_lossc() and max_series_loss() for custom tester metrics — these are backtest-only and not needed for live trading. Entry logic uses previous 3 bars of Fast TriX (V-bottom/inverted-V pattern) plus 2-bar momentum of Slow TriX as confirmation. New-bar guard uses tick_volume>1 check which is tick-data dependent.
